title: Which One's Deduction Show
notes: Detective-cast nodes (Heiji Hattori, Kazuha Toyama, Ran Mouri, Kogoro Mouri, Conan Edogawa, Inspector Megure, Takagi, Chiba) omitted by convention -- they drive the frame story (a Koushien-vs-Takarazuka bet) but are not case entities. case_type: murder. Discrepancies vs. the old cases/ file: (1) the victim's given name is spelled 'Kenji Tsujiya' in the old file, but the audio/subtitles clearly render it 'Tsujiya Kenshi' (Japanese name order) -- used 'Kenshi Tsujiya' here as the transcript-supported form. (2) The old file's culprit (s2, Hasami) is CORRECT -- matches the transcript. (3) The old file collapsed the entire dying-message mechanism into two flat clue/event stubs and, notably, mislabels object o2 as 'Borrowed shoes belonging to another suspect, used to frame him via video footage' while o3's clue text says the torn calendar 'ties directly back to him' (the culprit) without explaining why -- the actual mechanism is considerably more layered: the culprit (Hasami) blocked the tied-up victim's line of sight to the killer's face with the desk and a hidden video camera, then wore vice-president Iwatomi's stolen white golf shoes so the victim could only identify the killer by footwear; the culprit also deliberately (not accidentally) spilled ink near the victim -- proven because a genuine desk struggle would have also toppled the pen stand, and it didn't -- specifically so the victim could physically reach the scattered toy blocks and leave a dying message. The victim, honestly believing the shoes meant Iwatomi, stained blocks whose ink-marked faces spell nonsense ('o-mo-chi-ya') but whose fixed opposite faces (each block is a cube following the gojuon vowel-order, one block being the special ya-yu-yo-wa-wo-n line) decode to 'I-MI-TO-WA', an anagram of 'IWATOMI' -- a real, correctly-decoded dying message that nonetheless names the WRONG man, since Iwatomi has a solid TV-broadcast alibi (caught on camera at the golf tournament he claimed to attend). The real proof against Hasami is physical: blood wiped from his coat's left shoulder to a high wall calendar reachable only by someone of his height, plus his scent left inside the stolen shoes (confirmable by police dog). Motive was moral, not just the surface fear-of-being-fired story: Hasami opposed the president's and Iwatomi's cost-cutting decision to skip smoothing sharp corners on toys sold to children, and wanted Iwatomi specifically blamed and pushed out of toy production.

clues.desc: A genuine desk struggle would also have knocked over the idol-photo pen stand, but it's still upright -- proves the ink spill near the victim was deliberate, not a struggle accident.
The ink-stained block faces spell nonsense ('o-mo-chi-ya'), but each block's fixed opposite face decodes to 'I-MI-TO-WA' -- an anagram of IWATOMI.
Lined up at the wall calendar, only Hasami is tall enough for a shoulder-height blood smear to land where it did.
